Static --native-custody checker resolves the fixed path, cross-checks its framing/completeness and run/plan/config/native/source/input bindings against independent native records and frozen sources, and compares each child record to observer facts. Hashes inside custody protect byte consistency, not authenticity by themselves.
architecture.custody_location: Use fixed finalized {run_dir}/root-custody.json plus bounded observer launch/state partials in {run_dir}/root-custody/. Observer must finalize/fsync the custody file, exit, and be actually waited by the native-launched driver BEFORE that driver returns and native begins checking. Checker reads the finalized FILE and requires no live service contact. These are runtime output artifacts, not new repository source files. They reside outside execution/candidate, execution/baseline, shared/generator and all result trees. The observer alone writes bounded write-once observations/finalization; the source-pinned driver owns orchestration and never substitutes child stdout as custody.
architecture.explicit_trust: The source-pinned native driver and separate observer service, kernel /proc facts and root archival custody form the trusted local supervisor boundary. Solver children and their reseals are outside it. This is not a hostile-same-UID filesystem sandbox, privilege-separated service or cryptographic proof of all historical PIDs. Missing/false/unfinalized custody is a refusal; replacing the whole trusted boundary is an explicit out-of-scope compromise, never claimed defeated by selfhashes.
architecture.launch_barrier: Each generator/candidate/baseline lifecycle launch pauses at an explicit bounded ready/observation barrier before solver work. Driver reports the candidate PID only as a lookup hint. Observer independently obtains /proc PID/PPID/start_ticks/argv/boot/executable facts, checks ancestry to the observed native-launched driver and wrapper/target argv, hashes actual public input and all exact frozen source bytes itself, records the launch and acknowledges the bounded barrier. The child proceeds only after this acknowledgment. No child-supplied observation or hash is authoritative.
architecture.lifecycle: Observer service starts through existing fresh-thread-safe wrapper with expected-parent recheck/PDEATHSIG scope, uses bounded IPC/observation deadlines and handles source-pinned driver failure/expiry. Any observer start/finalization/death/timeout prevents success and prompts closure of all nested workers/service with retained partials. Actual native outer watchdog/authority expiry remains unchanged and is tested. No adopted waitpid acknowledgment is invented from ps absence/zombie state.

Service ancestry validation supplements these guards. architecture.selected_route: Native-launched driver keeps its existing production-authority parentPID/sys.orig_argv checks and starts a separate source-pinned observer.py service; no double inner production driver and no new source files.
architecture.service_start: After validating native launch/command/plan/environment/config/source authority, the native-launched source-pinned driver creates a dedicated private inherited IPC channel and starts observer.py service via the existing fresh lifecycle wrapper. The observer independently reads the native and driver /proc identities, validates parent ancestry/start/argv/boot identity against native launch.json/command.txt and bound plan/config. Solver/generator worker processes close fds and never inherit this service channel.
